findings.where: Desktop first screen: the 'write to me' note in the left margin
findings.fault: The page's only action is the smallest and most isolated thing in the first screen. It sits alone in the narrow margin, outside the reading column, with the double margin line between it and the heading and lede. It also floats below the italic experience line, lined up with no line of text. Squint at the screen and you see the heading, then the clipped photograph, then the large aqueduct sketch. The red note comes last, and it reads as a scribbled aside, not as the next step.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer who has just read who Mark is and wants to contact him. Their eye moves down the text column to the sketch and the style tile and never goes left to the margin, so they look for 'Contact' in the nav bar instead. Mark would object too, because getting in touch with him is the reason the homepage exists.

findings.where: Article page specimen: the PDF row ('Streamlining the PPP Process…' / 'Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF'), at desktop and phone
findings.fault: The row's bottom rule runs through the descenders of the last line of the title and of the date and format, instead of sitting below the text. It looks like a strike-through or an underline on the last line only, so the row's box doesn't close cleanly around its contents.
findings.who_objects: Angélique, who will add Mark's PDFs as rows like this one: every row she adds will look as if its last line is crossed out. A reader would object as well, because the rule makes it unclear where the link starts and ends.

findings.where: Article page specimen at desktop: the article title 'The World's Best Public- / Private Partnership Law', and the handwritten pull quote at both widths
findings.fault: The text snaps to the 32 px ruled lines, so the two-line title lands two rules apart. The gap between its lines is about as large as the type itself, and it reads as two separate headings. On the phone the same title is set tight. The pull quote likewise breaks into lines that stand far apart, three of them on the phone. On the template Mark's posts will use, the vertical rhythm comes from the ruled lines and not from the text, and it differs between widths.
findings.who_objects: A reader opening one of Mark's articles, who should take in the title at a glance but has to piece it together across the gap. Angélique would object too: any title long enough to wrap will break apart the same way.

findings.where: Palette section: the rows of swatches with their name, hex and role captions, at desktop and phone
findings.fault: The last caption line of one row ('ground', 'the stack', 'rules', 'margin, note') sits about as close to the next row's swatch as to its own. By proximity, each caption block floats between two swatches, and the rows run together into one undivided grid.
findings.who_objects: Mark or the founder reading the tile to choose a direction. On the phone especially, where the grid is two columns and four rows deep, they could match a role to the wrong colour.

findings.where: Motion sketch at phone width: the timeline table
findings.fault: The four-column table is kept at 390 px, so the Element column wraps one or two words to a line. The 'Hold' row runs to twelve short lines, with the Start, Length and Easing cells hanging at its top beside a long empty strip.
findings.who_objects: Mark, reviewing the tile on his phone: the timeline is hard to follow when each step is broken into a narrow column of fragments.
